svg.title: Global transport benchmark: control channels and media
svg.desc: Application control round-trip time and capture-to-decoded-frame media performance for self-hosted MoQ, PulseBeam, Cloudflare SFU, and the moq.dev public demo CDN from California to Virginia, Frankfurt, and Tokyo. A separately dated Cloudflare Managed MoQ extension is summarized without merging it into the matched matrix.
svg.text: Control + headless glass-to-glass media · California → Virginia / Frankfurt / Tokyo · latency and completion shown together

120 Hz control loss observed in 3/3 corridors
Verdict: self-hosted MoQ led the matched matrix; hosted-service extensions are reported separately.
Control: application RTT at 120 Hz, 5 min/provider/region. moq.dev control used latest-state groups and one pinned California ingress; its multi-edge qualification failed 0/600.
Media: capture-to-decoded-frame headless glass-to-glass proxy. moq.dev used per-frame fMP4 at conservative latency-max=100ms; failed attempts count against completion.
Do not compare control RTT numerically with one-way media latency. Camera exposure and display scanout are excluded. PulseBeam media is the disclosed 5 Mbps initial-BWE variant.
moq.dev is a public unauthenticated demo cluster, not a production SLA relay. Cloudflare Managed MoQ used a separately dated draft-14 extension.
